rows.inpatient_drg_scope: Inpatient/outpatient facility DRGs bundle routine room, nursing, and supplies; no separate reimbursement.

reimbursement_policies.evidence: Policy allows reimbursement for tracheostomy care supplies with conditions. In provider or facility settings, the supplies are included in the E&M visit or facility charge. In home health, they are separately reimbursed based on the applicable fee schedule or negotiated rate. One care kit per day is the default limit unless additional documentation supports more.

Tracheostomy care and listed tracheostomy/respiratory supplies are bundled into facility reimbursement. Routine nursing, room and board, and associated supplies are not separately reimbursed; only documented incremental nursing beyond standard care may be payable.

exemptions: incremental nursing charges with physician order and documentation

reimbursement_policies.evidence: This is a durable medical equipment policy focused on home-use equipment and supplies. It does not contain DRG inpatient payment rules for tracheostomy with prolonged mechanical ventilation or related inpatient outlier adjudication. Relevant respiratory items are addressed only as DME, oxygen, ventilators, and tracheostomy supplies for covered use cases.

reimbursement_policies.policy_title: Hospital Inclusive Charges Policy, Facility - Reimbursement Policy - UnitedHealthcare Commercial and Individual Exchange
reimbursement_policies.evidence: The payer's hospital inclusive-charges policy bundles routine tracheostomy care, respiratory therapy/nursing tasks, and routine ventilator/CPAP components into room, board, or facility charges. Facility-owned ventilator or CPAP management is reimbursable at one unit per day, but bundled components are not separately paid.
This is a general unlisted or miscellaneous code policy, not a DRG-specific reimbursement rule. It requires claim-by-claim review and supporting documentation when no established code exists.

Routine hospital supplies, services, equipment, and facility personnel are bundled into room and board charges and are not separately reimbursable; these items are also excluded from outlier calculations.

reimbursement_policies.policy_title: NF Ventilator Pre-Payment Medical Necessity Review
reimbursement_policies.evidence: Off-topic for this DRG pattern. The policy applies to nursing facility ventilator-dependent and ventilator-weaning services, with review of claims billed under revenue codes 0419 and 0410, rather than inpatient DRG payment for tracheostomy or respiratory outliers.

recommended_action.description:
Recommendation 1: Bundle facility-billed A4625 and related tracheostomy supply codes A4481, A4483, A4605, A4615-A4620, A4623, A4624, A4626, A4629, A7501-A7509, and A7520-A7527 under facility reimbursement when reported on revenue codes 0230-0239 on the same facility claim with routine room and board at the same level of care; keep an exception only for incremental nursing charges with physician order and documentation. Exempt: incremental nursing charges with physician order and documentation. Peer: Cigna and United Health both use same facility claim bundling as the trigger for inclusive facility charges..

Recommendation 2: Bundle ventilator or CPAP management to Hospital Inclusive Charges on UB04 inpatient facility claims and outpatient facility claims when billed on the same facility claim under revenue codes 260-269, 270, 279, 250, 300, 309, 361, 391, 410, or 412, and enforce the limit of 1 unit/day; apply this to bedside nurses, respiratory therapists, CNA, perfusionists, and technicians, while exempting facility-owned ventilator or CPAP management and ancillary ventilator or CPAP services. Exempt: facility-owned ventilator or CPAP management, ancillary ventilator or CPAP services. Peer: Cigna and United Health both use same facility claim bundling as the trigger for inclusive facility charges..
